bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs (device discovery, roles, decoding, exclusive grab); springboard/mcp/src/keys.rs (uinput virtual keyboard, agent tooling only)
summary: Core HID is a user-space API for discovering HID devices, reading their element values, sending reports and emulating virtual devices. BifrOSt has the kernel-side equivalent for its own shell: evdev discovery, classification of keyboards, pointers, touchscreens, power and lid devices, and a uinput keyboard for agent control. No SDK module exposes any of this to apps, and the framework's report-descriptor model is not implemented.

features.bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs (Device::by_name, InputSet with inotify watch on /dev/input at ~line 499)
features.note: Discovery runs inside the shell only. No SDK API lists devices for an app; springboard/sdk/src has no HID or device module.

features.bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs (Caps::roles at ~line 331, Roles struct above it)
features.note: Roles covers touchscreen, pointer, touchpad, keyboard, power and lid from evdev bits. There are no HID usage pages and no transport or localization codes.

Wave 2 (theme-18, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. BifrOSt never parses a HID report descriptor. It consumes the kernel's evdev translation.

features.bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs (Decoder at line 63 turns evdev records into touch and key events)
features.note: The values stay inside the shell. Apps get key and touch events through the window system, not HID values.

features.feature: Sending output reports to a device
features.apple: HIDDeviceClient (set report, for example an LED)
features.note: Wave 2 (theme-18, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Devices are read-only. Nothing sets LEDs, force feedback or feature reports.

features.apple: No direct counterpart; the framework's client model mediates access
features.note: The shell grabs its own input devices, never power buttons or lids. Apps have no way to grab a device.

features.bifrost: springboard/mcp/src/keys.rs (Keyboard::open, uinput keyboard for agent control); springboard/src/bare/input.rs (Device::virtual_device at line 152, a placeholder with fd -1)
features.note: The uinput keyboard is agent tooling, not an SDK API. It emulates a keyboard only, with no custom report descriptor and no delegate. The virtual_device constructor is a no-hardware stub for tests and headless runs.

features.bifrost: none; the shell's control port (springboard/src/bare/control.rs) exposes state, not device lists
features.note: A diagnostic dump of input devices exists only through the system layer and the observe tool. No documented command lists devices and their roles for a user.

gaps: No app-facing device manager: no SDK API lists HID devices, filters them by usage page or vendor, or reports hotplug to an app.
No report descriptor parsing (HIDElement, HIDElementCollection), so apps cannot read arbitrary HID devices such as custom controllers or instruments.
No output reports or feature reports (LED, force feedback, configuration) to devices.
No virtual HID device API for apps; the only virtual device is the agent uinput keyboard.
Transport and localization codes are not modelled.
